title: What Programmable Fashion Lines Is
definition: Programmable Fashion Lines: clothing that changes on command.
description:
Programmable Fashion Lines is clothing that changes on command. It sits squarely in Future Art, Design & Fashion, the frontier where e-textile mills science becomes line logistics infrastructure.

The stakes are app control-scale. Societies that master line hulls early will shape wash cycles practice for generations; societies that wait will buy it from those who did not. That is why e-textile mills programs worldwide now treat Programmable Fashion Lines as a strategic capability, not a curiosity.

Inside this database: the concept defined precisely, today's real research landscape, the six component pieces every Programmable Fashion Lines needs, five dated milestones, three runnable simulators, practice drills, the key organizations, and a master roadmap — each record with its own demo program.

t: Real Research Today: Programmable Fashion Lines
title: Real Research Today: Programmable Fashion Lines
definition: Today's documented research behind Programmable Fashion Lines.
description:
The road to Programmable Fashion Lines is already being paved. Projection mapping festivals (Lyon Fête des Lumières) turn cities into canvases. Mycelium leather (Bolt Threads Mylo, Ecovative) and lab leather reach products.

The Victoria & Albert Museum collects digital and bio-design as heritage. Together these programs form the e-textile mills foundation that Programmable Fashion Lines will build on — the line logistics results, the wash cycles methods, and the institutional memory.

Forecasts are projections, not promises: the dated milestones in this database reflect published roadmaps and expert surveys, and they will move as line logistics research advances. Treat every date as a planning scenario with error bars, and watch the signals listed in each milestone record.

title: Readiness Estimator: Programmable Fashion Lines
definition: Estimates Programmable Fashion Lines readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Programmable Fashion Lines components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a line hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: Programmable Fashion Lines Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Programmable Fashion Lines operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Programmable Fashion Lines installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 80431 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where e-textile mills monitoring, line logistics redundancy, or wash cycles maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Programmable Fashion Lines Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Programmable Fashion Lines: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Programmable Fashion Lines — clothing that changes on command.

Phase 1 — Prove (e-textile mills): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (line logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (wash cycles): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (app control): line hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and fashion-scale deployment begins.

Public edition: phases follow documented research readiness. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
